facts.fact: Blue (18, Walter Travis), White (9) and Red (9) courses, opened in stages 1921-1925, on National Park Service land at Hains Point.
Some of the city's oldest Japanese flowering cherry trees grow in East Potomac Park; its mini golf (1931) is the oldest continuously operated in the US.

current.subject: The domed, columned memorial; the three courses on Blue, White and Red discs.
current.keep: The memorial, and the colour system for the three courses.
current.weaknesses: The dome fills the disc; columns are lost; the rims are thin.

concepts.name: The Memorial across the Basin
concepts.rationale: A cleaner memorial (dome, pediment, six columns, steps) over the Tidal Basin. The courses get a navy field with a thick Blue, White or Red rim.
references: The Jefferson Memorial across the Tidal Basin
concepts.symbolism: Golf in the shadow of the monuments.
concepts.strengths: A dignified family; the rim colour tells the courses apart at 1x.

concepts.name: Hains Point Blossom
concepts.rationale: A five-petal cherry blossom on the same navy field and coloured rims.
references: Cherry trees of East Potomac Park (fact)
concepts.strengths: Beautiful and readable; the same rim system.
concepts.tradeoffs: Cherry blossoms are the city's symbol, not only the park's.

recommendation: Concept 1. The memorial with coloured rims is the clearest system for three courses.
